# Fig. 2 — Hierarchical control structure of one VSM-controlled DFIG

**Section 2.1** · the five control elements and their interconnections.

**Status: `verified`.** A drawing, not a computed result. Every block it shows
is checked against the code below.

---

## This figure is not generated by the code

`controlDiagram-2_bold_new.pdf`, hand-drawn. What is verifiable is the
correspondence between what it shows and what the model implements.

## The five elements, and where each lives

| Element | Purpose | Design parameters | Code |
|---|---|---|---|
| **VSMP** | Swing equation, active power and frequency | `H`, `D_p`, `D_d` | `CONTROL/CONFIG_CONTROL.m` |
| **VSMQ** | Virtual flux, stator voltage magnitude | `D_q`, `K_q` | idem |
| **RSC d/q** | Rotor current, torque and rotor reactive power | `φ_m`, `ω_o`, `b` | idem |
| **VDC** | DC-link voltage | `φ_m`, `ω_o`, `b` | idem |
| **GSC d/q** | Grid-side converter current | `φ_m`, `ω_o`, `b` | idem |

Plus the **virtual impedance**, which is not a loop but modifies the VSMQ
reference. See below.

## Naming, which the figure gets wrong

> **The virtual-flux loop is labelled "VMSQ" in the diagram. It is the VSMQ loop
> of the text and of Tables 3–7.** A transposition, not a different block.

## Six loops carry a phase margin, not seven

VSMQ has no phase-margin specification: the droop structure fixes it, which is
why Section 4.1.2 optimises only its crossover frequency and why the feasibility
test of Section 4.1.4 counts **six** loops.

Counting seven is the commonest way to get the feasibility test wrong.

## The virtual impedance sits inside the VSMQ reference

Not a separate loop. The rotor current reference is formed as

```
irdq_ref = 1/Lm · (Fs_ref − Lv·it_dq − Ls·is_dq)
```

`it_dq` is the **complete dq phasor**, so `L_v` multiplies real and imaginary
parts alike. In the linear analysis it appears as two equations, one per axis,
both carrying `L_v`.

It is a virtual inductance inside the stator-flux reference of the VSMQ loop,
acting on both axes.

The virtual resistance is zero: the virtual impedance is the inductance `L_v`
alone. See [`tab05_optimized_params.md`](tab05_optimized_params.md).

## The RSC references are not exogenous, and this has consequences

The figure shows `isp_rdq` computed from the stator current `is`, the total
output current into the feeder `ildq`, the rotor electrical speed and the VSM
angle. **That is a feedback path, not a reference path.**

Consequence, measured: a 2-DOF setpoint weight applied to those references
**enters the state matrix**. Phase 3 of the optimisation moves three such
weights and the state matrices differ in 506 of 6400 entries, shifting the MF
damping minimum by 3.3 %.

Equation (1) of the paper should not be read as implying the weights are
confined to the reference path. A reimplementation that routes them as pure
feedforward will find Phase 3 does nothing. See
[`tab08_phase_progression.md`](tab08_phase_progression.md).

## What the figure does not show

The four protection mechanisms of Section 2.2 — current limiters, DC-link
chopper, RSC derate, diode clamp. They are absent from the diagram because they
are absent from the **design configuration**, which is what the diagram
describes. They exist in the model and are disabled by default. See
[`00_setup.md`](00_setup.md).
